build.summary:
I made all three repairs. The four acceptance test files pass and the typecheck is clean. One test file outside this package now fails: src/ui/access/caseTips.reach.test.ts, which a different package owns. That failure is the expected result of moving the two cold-leg tips; its own comment says it should fail when they move. I left it alone and describe the fix under outOfScope.

(1) Launch fixture tests in src/content/content.test.ts. The fixture lesson, module and case are now added to the full TRACKS and PUBLISHED_CASES instead of replacing them with a one-lesson track. The real .launch.ts files are therefore checked against the whole curriculum, and any error a fixture test sees comes from the fixture. I added two tests:
- With the fixture lab file loaded and no fixture content, the full curriculum gives no errors.
- A bad .launch.ts that names an unknown lesson, an unknown case and an unknown scenario produces exactly those four errors. The same file also names the last lesson of the last track, and that reference is accepted, which shows the check uses the full TRACKS.

(2) Tie-break in src/content/lab/tips.ts. I added an exported tipSpecificity(tip, ctx), which returns two counts:
- conditions: one for each trigger field that is set, plus one for every required event.
- breadth: the total number of entries in the trigger's lists (phase, event, catheter and so on), plus the number of steps in a step range. Borrowed tips are measured by the phases of their alsoIn entry.

tipsFor now sorts by score first. Equal scores go by more conditions, then fewer alternatives, then caution or bailout ahead of do, then registry order. The tone bonus stays in the score, so a warning tip still always beats a do tip it outscores. tipsForAll sorts by score, then the context where the tip scored best, then specificity, then registry order, and with one context it gives the same result as tipsFor. Both docstrings describe the rule.

pci-eqb-standard-first now ranks 14th in the equipment test's own calcified-RCA scenario context (it was 20th, just outside the top 20), 14th for lesion-prep with balloon-uncrossable alone (was 20th), and 19th for the hand-made calcified RCA context (was 25th).

(3) In src/content/lab/raisable/waiting.ts, I moved access-cx-cold-leg-six-ps and access-closure-cold-leg from the proc-tip-context group to the access-cx-endovascular-control group, with a note saying why. The file's format is unchanged and reachability.test.ts passes.

Before editing, I snapshotted the four files under datasets/tmp/wp-snapshots/repair-launch-fixture-and-tip-ties/ and created the .started marker there.

build.notes:
The tie-break never overrides the score, so a caution or bailout tip still beats any do tip it outscores. The explicit tone key only matters if a future weight change makes a warning and a do tip tie on score.

tipsForAll keeps "context first, then specificity" so that it still follows caseTips.ts's documented merge order (score, then context, then registry). I did not change caseTips.ts, which belongs to another package. If that file merges tips itself, its order within a tie may now differ from tipsForAll's, but caseTips.test.ts still passes.

The fingerprint-gated snapshot test in tips.test.ts is still skipped, because the tip data no longer matches the recorded fingerprint. I reworded it to compare the tip set and scores so it stays correct if the fingerprint ever matches again.

I did not use the browser or start a dev server. The scratch scripts I used to check rankings are in the session scratchpad, not the project.

findings.fix: Replace the registry-wide loop with an assertion of the property that actually guarantees the ordering. Then for each consecutive pair in tipsFor(ctx, 1000) where out[i].tone === 'do' and out[i+1].tone !== 'do', expect tipScore(out[i]) to be greater than tipScore(out[i+1]). Rename the synthetic test to say the ordering comes from the tone bonus in the score, or keep it and add a line to compareTied's docstring that the tone key is defensive and unreachable under current weights.

review.verdict:
Approve, with follow-ups outside this package. All three repairs are implemented completely and correctly.

(1) content.test.ts now checks the real .launch.ts files against the full TRACKS and PUBLISHED_CASES, with the fixture content added on top. A new fixture test shows that an unknown lesson, case or scenario is rejected, with exactly four errors. It also shows that the last lesson of the last track is accepted, so the check really uses the full curriculum (TRACKS has more than ten tracks).

(2) tips.ts adds an exported tipSpecificity and a documented compareTied. Sort order: score, then more conditions, then fewer alternatives, then caution or bailout ahead of do, then registry index. tipsForAll keeps the context key before specificity. Score always comes first, so the shared engine's default limit and scoring are unchanged and only the order within a tie changes. The cost is a few array reads per matching tip per call, not per frame. Registry tests show pci-eqb-standard-first inside the top 20 at lesion-prep with balloon-uncrossable.

(3) waiting.ts moves only the two cold-leg ids, into the existing access-cx-endovascular-control group, with a note that keeps the file's format. The tips' triggers (phase including 'complication', event limb-ischaemia, femoral) match that package's tipIntegration in the plan.

Verified myself: the four acceptance files pass (103 passed, 1 skipped), and npx tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit exits 0. Downstream tip consumers all pass: retarget, scenarios/tips, equipment.tips, handover, multiSite.tips, caseTips, diagnosticContext, diagnosticTips, haemoTips, labRun, patientEvents, physiologyTips, useContextTips and script. The one exception is src/ui/access/caseTips.reach.test.ts, which fails one test as the builder predicted. It belongs to proc-tip-context and needs a two-line fix.

Other src files modified after .started: mentor/*, simulation/access/route.ts, ui/access/AccessFluoroView.tsx, UltrasoundView.tsx, AccessPicker.tsx, session/caseSession.ts, autopilot.ts, multiSite.test.ts, sections/Settings*, physics/types.test.ts. All plausibly belong to other packages (route.ts and AccessFluoroView.tsx to access-cx-endovascular-control, caseSession.ts to proc-tip-context), and none is attributable to this package.

The package adds no clinical numbers, UI or live-screen ground truth. The test weaknesses are minor: the tone tie-break test cannot fail, because the 0.5 tone bonus makes warning and do scores impossible to tie, and caseTips.ts's own merge does not yet use the new tie-break.

fix.notes:
I applied two findings.

Finding 3 (the tone tests could not fail): this was correct. Every term in tipScore is a whole number except the +0.5 tone bonus, so a caution or bailout tip can never tie a do tip on score. The tone key in compareTied therefore never takes effect under today's weights. I made three changes in src/content/lab/tips.test.ts and src/content/lab/tips.ts:
- I replaced the registry-wide double loop with a test of the property that actually guarantees the order. For every matching tip in each context, the score ends in .5 exactly when the tone is not 'do'. For each adjacent pair in tipsFor(ctx, 1000) where a do tip comes just before a warning, the do tip has the strictly higher score. The test also asserts that at least one such pair exists, so this second check is not empty.
- I renamed the synthetic test to say the ordering comes from the tone bonus in the score.
- I added a line to the compareTied docstring saying the tone key is defensive and cannot be reached under the current weights. It keeps the rule if the weights change.

Finding 5 (src/content/lab/raisable/waiting.ts header): I added repair-launch-fixture-and-tip-ties (the cold-leg move) to the list of packages that edit the file. The data is unchanged and reachability.test.ts still passes.

Findings 1, 2 and 4 are correct, but they are in files owned by other packages, so I did not touch them. The fixes are under rejected, for the coordinator to pass on. Finding 1 matters most: src/ui/access/caseTips.reach.test.ts stays red until proc-tip-context updates it.
